objectives: Pupils can ask simple questions about a family member using he/she: How old is she? What is his name? Is he your brother?
Pupils can answer questions about a family member with short statements using he/she
Pupils can hold a short partner interview about a family member in English without notes

stages.name: Opening and retrieval
stages.purpose: Activate Aug 19 family descriptions at free-recall level and create a felt need to ask about family members, bridging into today's new input.

procedure.text: Place 4 picture-word cards on the board: mother, father, sister, brother. Quick oral drill -- point to each card and ask 'Who is this?' Pupils answer as a class.
Write 2 sentences about a family member (real or imaginary) using he or she. Include name and age. Example structure: 'This is my [relation]. His/Her name is [name]. He/She is [age] years old.'
Ask 2-3 pupils to share. Write one strong example on the board: 'This is my brother. His name is Max. He is 9 years old.' Leave this on the board for reference.
Bridge: 'You can now tell me about your family. But what if I want to ask you about them? Today you learn how to ask.' Point to the example on the board and mime questioning -- 'How old is he?'

stages.name: Grammar input: Asking about someone else
stages.purpose: Introduce question inversion with he/she -- swapping 'is' and the person word -- using before/after examples and German L1 comparison to build confidence.

procedure.text: Display the grammar intro material. Read the rule aloud. Walk through each before/after example: 'She is my sister' becomes 'Is she your sister?' Point out: 'is' jumps to the front. Then show the German parallel: 'Wie alt ist sie?' = 'How old is she?' -- same flip in both languages.
Echo practice in pairs: Teacher says a statement, pupils say the matching question. Three rounds -- 'He is 8.' / 'She is from London.' / 'His name is Ben.'
Write question starters on board -- pupils copy into their notebooks: How old is...? / What is...? / Where is...? / Is he...? / Is she...?

stages.name: Guided practice
stages.purpose: Consolidate he/she statement and question forms through two progressive exercises: Band 1 gap-fill with full word bank, then Band 2 sentence reorder without a word bank.

procedure.text: Hand out or display the gap-fill exercise. Show the word bank: is, How old, Where, What. Read item 1 aloud as a model. Remind pupils: 'Use the word bank -- every word there is used at least once.'
Read answers aloud. Pupils self-check. For each question item, ask: 'Which word came first? Why?' -- brief oral explanation reinforces the inversion rule.
Display the reorder exercise. Explain: 'The words are scrambled. Put them in the right order to make a question or sentence. No word bank this time -- use what you remember.'
Pairs swap and check each other's answers. Then whole-class confirm item 2 ('Is he your brother?') -- common point of confusion: 'Is' must come first.

stages.name: Oral pair work: Family interview
stages.purpose: Produce questions and short answers about a family member in free oral interaction, building fk.k.sprechen.1 at produce depth.

procedure.text: Model the task with one pupil. Teacher is Partner B (questioner). Pupil describes a family member; teacher asks at least 2 questions using the board starters. Then swap roles briefly. Keep the question starters visible on the board throughout.

In pairs: Partner A describes one family member (real or imaginary -- name, age, and one more fact). Partner B asks at least 2 questions. Then switch. Sentence frames stay on the board. Stronger pupils: cover the board with their hand when speaking.
2-3 pairs share one exchange with the class. After each, ask: 'Was the question correct? What did they say?' Light whole-class error check -- focus on word order only.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Close with a learning intention check so pupils leave with a clear sense of what they can now do.

procedure.text: Read the 'I can...' statement on the board together: 'I can ask and answer simple questions about a family member in English.' Ask: thumbs up (yes, confident), thumbs sideways (almost), thumbs down (need more practice).
Pupils show their thumb. Mentally note any thumbs-down -- those pupils get priority support in the next lesson's review.
Announce homework: 'Write 3 sentences about a family member at home. Use the sheet.' Preview the task quickly -- 30 seconds.

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: sentence frames stay on the board for the full oral stage; they may also refer to the gap-fill answer key during pair work. Stronger pupils: cover the board during oral production; as an extension, ask a third question not on the board (e.g. 'Does he/she have a pet?'). For pupils who showed thumbs-down in the Aug 19 wrap-up: seat them near the board and prompt with the question starters before the oral stage begins.
exercisePlan: Band 1 gap-fill: fill in is / How old / Where / What in family descriptions and questions, full word bank provided
Band 2 reorder: reconstruct scrambled he/she questions from fragments, no word bank
